scenes.title: Cardamom Rolls for Diplomacy
scenes.summary: On Monday morning, F2 packs a linen-lined basket of warm cardamom-almond rolls while coaching M2 and F1 for their diplomatic visit to Number Twelve.
scenes.intro: Bright Monday morning sunshine fills the café corner of {SHOW}. {F2} tucks six fragrant cardamom-almond knots into a woven basket lined with crisp linen while {F1} and {M2} rehearse their opening greeting. Listen first.
story: F2
Six warm cardamom-almond knots, zero plum jam anywhere in sight—pure culinary diplomacy!
M2
Thoughtful touch, {F2}; mentioning plums inside Number Twelve might set diplomacy back fifty years.
F1
Let us review our three talking points before we ring her street bell, {M2}.
M2
Point One: introduce ourselves warmly as neighbours who admire traditional ceramic craftsmanship.
F1
Point Two: explain gently that rainwater is dripping onto the shared eighteen-ninety conservatory tiles.
F2
And Point Three: offer our expert skylight repair at zero expense to her!
M2
Simple, gracious, and completely foolproof—where did I lay my clean handkerchief?
F1
In your left pocket, {M2}, and your reading glasses are still safely on your nose!
F2
Remember to listen twice as much as you speak once she opens the door, boss.
M2
Nobody listens more patiently than I do when historic architecture is at stake!
F1
Basket in my hands, postal map copy tucked neatly underneath—ready for ten cobblestones?
M2
Shoulders straight, {F1}; let us go knock on Number Twelve!
scenes.outro: Armed with warm cardamom bread and three sensible talking points, {F1} and {M2} step next door into uncharted territory! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Cracked Sign Story
scenes.summary: Returning from Number Twelve twenty minutes later, F1 and M2 tell F3 that their neighbour accepted the rolls warmly—yet refused to sign over a broken 1890 porcelain sign.
scenes.intro: Twenty minutes later, {F1} and {M2} return to the front desk carrying an empty bread basket and thoughtful expressions as {F3} steps in from her morning walk. Let us listen in first.
story: F3
An empty bread basket is a promising sign—how did the ceramic restorer receive you?
F1
She was remarkably gracious, {F3}, and praised {F2} and her cardamom dough right away!
M2
Until I politely mentioned co-signing the Municipal Vault release for our shared conservatory keys.
F3
Oh dear—did the old plum tart misunderstanding resurface after all these decades, {M2}?
F1
Not the tart at all! She told us a completely different story from forty years ago.
M2
Apparently their old six-tile cobalt porcelain shop sign fell off the shared boundary wall!
F3
How dreadful for a family of ceramic artists—did the tiles shatter on the cobbles?
F1
Worse: she believes our upper copper rainwater spout broke loose and knocked those tiles down!
M2
And when her father looked outside the next morning, every single blue tile had vanished!
F3
Wait—she thinks someone from {SHOW} swept away their heirloom porcelain sign without apologizing?!
F1
She said until our house accounts honestly for that gutter and sign, the arch stays bolted.
M2
Call {M1} and {M3} up to the balcony—we need forensic gutter evidence immediately!
scenes.outro: Forget the plum tart—the real wound next door is a vanished six-tile porcelain sign from forty years back! See you on the balcony next time.

scenes.title: Clues on the Copper Spout
scenes.summary: Up on the east corner of the balcony, M1 and M3 inspect the original copper downpipe and prove {SHOW}'s gutter never touched Number Twelve's sign wall.
scenes.intro: Out on the sunny east end of the upper balcony, {M1} and {M3} lean carefully over the oak rail to examine the nineteenth-century copper rainwater pipe along the party wall. Listen first.
story: M3
Look at the bronze masonry brackets holding our copper downpipe, {M1}—original eighteen-ninety ironwork.
M1
Neither bent nor patched; this pipe has not shifted five millimetres in a hundred years.
M3
Now sight straight down the party wall toward the street corner between both gates.
M1
Aha—do you see those two rusted iron hooks bolted directly above her stone lintel?
M3
And look thirty centimetres higher: an old ceramic insulator bracket from the street tramway wire!
M1
Wait a minute—forty years ago the city removed the overhead tram cables along {STREET}!
M3
When the municipal crew unbolted that heavy steel cable, vibration shook the lintel mortar loose!
M1
So our copper gutter was completely innocent—the street tram crew dislodged those hooks!
M3
That explains how the sign fell, {M1}, yet why did all six blue tiles disappear overnight?
M1
Hold everything... forty years ago, did the aunt of {M2} not sweep here at six?!
M3
If she found six loose tiles in the rain at dawn, would she discard them?
M1
Never in a million years—come check the top shelf of the back hallway cupboard!
scenes.outro: Old tramway hooks clear {SHOW}'s copper pipe—and spark a hunch about what {M2}'s careful aunt rescued at dawn! See you downstairs next time.

scenes.title: Wrapped in Old Newspaper
scenes.summary: On the highest shelf of the back hallway cupboard, M1 lifts down a wooden tea crate holding six intact blue-and-white porcelain tiles wrapped in newspaper.
scenes.intro: Setting his wooden step-stool inside the back hallway cupboard, {M1} reaches past the old soup kettle lid to lift down a small nailed cedar tea chest for {F1} and {F3}. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
Look at the faded pencil label across the cedar lid: Fragile Blue Street Tiles—Keep Safe!
M1
Tucked all the way behind the winter blankets where nobody reached for forty years.
F3
Gently lift the top layer of yellowed newspaper, {F1}—is anything shattered inside?
F1
Tile one... unbroken! Tile two... unbroken! Cobalt-blue brushwork on creamy white porcelain glaze!
M1
Count the rest underneath the wood shavings: three, four, five, and six whole tiles!
F3
Wait—look at this folded slip of note paper written in that familiar neat calligraphy!
F1
Read what she wrote on the morning she rescued them from the wet pavement, {F3}!
F3
Found beside gate after night storm; clean mortar off backs and return when neighbours speak again.
M1
She wrapped each tile individually so not a single glazed corner would chip.
F1
Then she fell ill that winter, and nobody knew whose sign lay inside this chest!
F3
Imagine her face next door seeing that hand-painted porcelain sign whole after forty years!
M1
Carry them gently into Room Nine—let us inspect the backs before anyone touches mortar.
scenes.outro: Rescued from a stormy pavement forty years ago, all six cobalt porcelain tiles emerge unbroken from newspaper! See you in Room 9 next time.

scenes.title: The Number on Tile Six
scenes.summary: In Room 9, M4 arrives with the Municipal Vault requirements just as F1 and M3 spot the missing joint-deposit tally number pencilled on the back of tile six!
scenes.intro: At one in the afternoon inside bright Room 9, {F1} and {M3} lay the six cobalt porcelain tiles face-up on green velvet just as {M4} walks in carrying an official cream folder from City Hall. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Whoa—where on earth did you unearth six museum-grade nineteenth-century cobalt tiles?!
F1
Up on our hallway shelf! Put together, they read: Twin Courtyards Kiln and Bakehouse!
M3
And we proved from the tramway bracket upstairs that our gutter never knocked them down!
M4
Incredible timing, because the Municipal Vault clerk gave me good news AND a catch.
F1
Good news first, {M4}—did the clerk locate Envelope Fourteen-AB in the basement safe?
M4
Both eighteen-ninety wrought-iron keys are sitting inside, tagged and rust-free since nineteen-sixty-six!
M3
Now tell us the bureaucratic catch before we celebrate too soon, big brother.
M4
Besides both owners signing this form, someone must quote the five-digit green tally number!
F1
A five-digit tally number from sixty years ago?! Where could anyone find THAT?!
M3
Wait a second—turn Tile Number Six over slowly on the velvet cloth, {F1}!
F1
Written in waterproof glazing crayon across the unglazed biscuit clay: Vault Tally Four-Eight-Nine-One-Two!
M4
Her grandfather recorded his vault code on the back of his prized doorway tile!
scenes.outro: Glazing crayon on nineteenth-century clay delivers the exact five-digit vault code needed at City Hall! See you in the courtyard next time.

scenes.title: Step Away with That Glue
scenes.summary: In the courtyard, M1 stops M2 two seconds before he squeezes modern instant glue onto the 1890 porcelain tiles, teaching him how breathable lime mortar protects antique clay.
scenes.intro: Out at courtyard worktable two, {M2} uncaps a shiny silver tube of hardware-store instant glue near the six antique tiles—until {M1} steps between him and the table beside {F2}. Listen first.
story: M2
Stand back, everyone—in sixty seconds flat I shall glue all six tiles onto plywood!
M1
Drop that tube of chemical superglue right now, boss, or I confiscate your apron.
F2
Thank goodness you walked out, {M1}! Tell him what synthetic glue does to antique clay!
M1
Hard plastic glue traps moisture behind nineteenth-century glaze until the porcelain face cracks clean off.
M2
Cracks the glaze?! Put the cap back on tightly—keep that tube ten metres away!
F2
How do real ceramic restorers mount heavy exterior sign tiles safely, {M1}?
M1
Soft slaked lime putty mixed with fine washed sand inside a seasoned cedar cradle.
M2
Wait—the woman next door IS a retired ceramic restorer; she will inspect every joint!
M1
Which is why {M3} and {M4} are mitring a mortised cedar frame with brass clips.
F2
No glue, zero chemical fumes, and removable whenever a restorer wants to clean the backs!
M2
Allow me to carry the washed sand bucket humbly while true craftsmen handle the tiles!
M1
Now you are talking like an owner worthy of a magazine cover, boss.
scenes.outro: Rescued from instant superglue, the six cobalt tiles await an authentic cedar cradle and breathable lime bed! See you next time.

scenes.title: Framing the Six Tiles
scenes.summary: Under the shade tree, M3 and M4 fit the six porcelain tiles snugly into a hand-planed cedar frame with brass corner clasps while F3 polishes the cobalt glaze.
scenes.intro: Late Monday afternoon beneath the courtyard tree, {M3} and {M4} slide the sixth cobalt-and-white tile gently into a grooved red-cedar frame while {F3} buffs the surface with a soft chamois cloth. Listen first.
story: M4
Slide the brass retaining bar home on the right edge—snug without pinching the clay!
M3
Two millimetres of cork expansion cushion all around so winter and summer air never bind.
F3
Look how the deep cobalt lettering gleams once forty years of cupboard dust lift away!
M4
Twin Courtyards Kiln and Bakehouse—painted by hand before motorcars ever drove down {STREET}!
M3
And we copied Vault Tally Four-Eight-Nine-One-Two onto the City Hall release form first.
F3
Who should carry this cedar frame next door tomorrow morning at ten, gentlemen?
M4
{M2} and {F1} started the conversation today, so they deserve to finish it.
M3
Plus {F1} drew a neat diagram of the old tramway bracket to explain how it fell!
F3
Truth, craftsmanship, and forty-year-old kindness—how could any heart on {STREET} resist that?
M4
As soon as she signs line two tomorrow morning, I sprint straight to the Municipal Vault!
M3
Which means by Tuesday sunset, both eighteen-ninety iron keys could be back home!
F3
Rest well tonight, builders; tomorrow sixty years of silence finally meet fresh air!
scenes.outro: Cushioned in cork and oiled cedar, the six-tile heirloom gleams like 1890 ahead of Tuesday morning's knock! One final scene in Episode 2!

scenes.title: Tears at Number Twelve
scenes.summary: At ten-thirty Tuesday morning, F1 and M2 return jubilantly to the café corner with a signed vault release after restoring the framed porcelain sign to a deeply moved neighbour.
scenes.intro: Half past ten Tuesday morning! {F1} and {M2} burst back into the sunny café corner waving a signed cream City Hall form before an eager {F2}. Listen first.
story: F2
LOOK AT THOSE SMILES! Tell me what happened when you unveiled the cedar tile frame!
F1
For ten seconds she could not speak—just traced the cobalt kiln with one finger!
M2
Then she recognized the cedar cradle and praised our cork expansion joints like a master!
F2
Did you show her that pencilled note from the stormy morning forty years ago, {M2}?
M2
She read it twice, wiped away a tear, and apologized for blaming our copper gutter!
F1
And when {M2} apologized for that ancestral plum tart temper, they both burst out laughing!
F2
Wait—did she actually sign line two of the Municipal Vault joint-release paper?!
F1
Signed in bold black fountain ink AND confirmed Tally Number Four-Eight-Nine-One-Two from memory!
M2
Even better: she promised to meet us on her side of the arch at five today!
F2
{M4} is waiting by the gate on his bicycle to rush this form downtown!
F1
Hand it over quickly—by five this afternoon, both iron keys turn together!
M2
Sixty summers of stubbornness ended over six blue tiles and warm cardamom bread!
scenes.outro: Laughter replaces a sixty-year feud, the joint release speeds downtown, and a five-sharp appointment awaits at the 1890 arch! End of Episode 2—see you in Episode 3!
